kf: **Purpura** is bleeding into the skin that does **not blanch**: petechiae (<2 mm), purpura (2–10 mm), ecchymoses (>1 cm).
**Non-blanching rash in an unwell or febrile child: meningococcal sepsis until proven otherwise** (NICE NG240: benzylpenicillin, 999).
Flat purpura: platelets, clotting, vessel fragility (steroids, age, scurvy); palpable purpura: vasculitis.
Tests: FBC and film, clotting, U&E, LFT, CRP, blood cultures if febrile; urine and BP for vasculitis.
Consider leukaemia (petechiae, pallor, bone pain), ITP, anticoagulants and non-accidental injury in children.
myths: **"The glass test is negative so it's fine"**: early meningococcal rash may blanch; judge the whole child.
patho_lead: Purpura means **red cells outside vessels**: from low platelets, clotting defects, fragile or inflamed vessels.

mech.t: Low or dysfunctional platelets cause petechiae and mucosal bleeding.
Clotting factor deficiency causes larger bruises and deep bleeds.
Thin dermis (age, steroids) or weak collagen (scurvy) lets vessels tear: senile purpura.
Inflamed vessels leak red cells, causing raised palpable purpura.
mech.cap: Vasculitis: neutrophils damage small vessels and red cells leak into the dermis.

comp: Depends on cause: sepsis, haemorrhage, organ damage.
